title: Um Jammer Lammy
subtitle: Late for the first concert
summary: Um Jammer Lammy is NanaOn-Sha's PlayStation rhythm game, released in Japan on 18 March 1999. body: Um Jammer Lammy is NanaOn-Sha's PlayStation rhythm game, released in Japan on 18 March 1999. Lammy, the nervous guitarist of MilkCan, has fifteen minutes to reach her band's concert, but a succession of absurd emergencies blocks the way. Imagining an object as a guitar helps her find the confidence to respond. Masaya Matsuura's musical design again meets Rodney Alan Greenblat's flat, colourful characters, following their work on PaRappa the Rapper. This time the performance is built around guitar phrases, with each interruption becoming another unlikely stage on the way to the real one.

A teacher performs a phrase, then Lammy answers through button presses on a scrolling score. Following the pattern keeps the song moving; well-timed improvisation can earn more points and raise the performance from Good to Cool. At that rank, the teacher leaves and the player can keep developing a personal response, provided the rhythm remains convincing. Poor playing lowers the rank and can end the song. The contest therefore asks for more than mechanical repetition: the printed notes establish a phrase that can become a starting point for another variation.

Unlockable effects change Lammy's guitar with distortion, flanging, reverb and other treatments. Shoulder buttons operate a whammy effect, while some settings respond to analogue control. These sound changes are optional and do not increase the score, leaving room to experiment simply because the result is enjoyable. Completing Lammy's story also opens PaRappa's versions of the songs, and multiplayer extends the call-and-response idea to another person. Regional versions changed one episode's setting, but the journey retains its central joke: a shy character repeatedly discovers that she can play her way through the obstruction in front of her.
